where: Section 3 (partial fractions and the cover-up shortcut)
problem: The cover-up instruction is wrong. If G(x) = P(x)/Q(x) = A₁/(1 − a₁x) + A₂/(1 − a₂x) + ⋯, then multiplying through by Q(x) gives P(x) = A₁Q(x)/(1 − a₁x) + A₂Q(x)/(1 − a₂x) + ⋯. Putting x = 1/aᵢ does not isolate Aᵢ — it gives P(1/aᵢ) = Aᵢ·∏_{j≠i}(1 − a_j/aᵢ). A student following this step in an exam gets an answer off by the factor ∏_{j≠i}(1 − a_j/aᵢ).
fix: Multiply both sides only by (1 − aᵢx), the factor belonging to Aᵢ, and then put x = 1/aᵢ. All other terms still contain (1 − aᵢx) and vanish, leaving Aᵢ = [(1 − aᵢx)·G(x)] evaluated at x = 1/aᵢ. That is the cover-up shortcut. (Equivalently, cancel (1 − aᵢx) out of Q(x) before substituting.)

problem: The last sentence gives the wrong reason. No term is missing because the shifted index k runs from 0 upward, so the sum is over the whole sequence; this is true whatever index the recurrence starts at. A reader can take away that the completeness depends on the recurrence starting at n = 1, which is not so.
fix: Replace the last sentence with: the shifted index k covers 0, 1, 2, …, the entire sequence, so no term of G(x) is lost, and the factor x stands outside the sum.
